alignments.note: Causal ὅτι rendered by the clause-introducing For.
Comparative καθώς keeps only as; the correlative even so belongs to the expressed οὕτως under rule 82.
Article to the (rule 19); split from its noun under rule 13.
Article before a name with no English determiner (rules 21, 23); the case preposition of stays with the noun, since rule 21 forbids leaving a bare of on the article.
Genitive noun rendered of + noun; head on the noun (rule 17).

οὕτως takes even so, headed on so, the supplied even an intensifying helper (rule 82, which names οὕτως → even so as this very case). Giving even to καί discontinuously is the competing reading, but rule 82 settles even so as one unit on the adverb and καί has its own also.
Article displaced by the possessive our, which belongs to the expressed genitive ἡμῶν (rule 20); by rule 76's test that genitive is unspent and so available to carry it.
Genitive pronoun realized by the possessive our.
Adjunctive καί to also, standing where the Greek does before the noun phrase; the correlative so is already οὕτως's.
Article before a name with no English realization (rule 23).

review_notes: Reviewed against the contract and returned unchanged. Partition verified: all 18 source and all 17 target IDs are used exactly once, and every head is a member of its own array.

Both περισσεύει tokens are separately aligned to their own English verbs, abound and aboundeth. The ASV reverses the order of the second clause (aboundeth through Christ for διὰ τοῦ Χριστοῦ περισσεύει), but rule 15 licenses that reordering without merging anything, and rule 26 forbids bundling the transparent pieces.

καθώς / οὕτως / καί: rule 82 keeps a bare as on καθώς, gives the correlative even so to the expressed οὕτως headed on so, and leaves the adjunctive καί its own also. Rule 82's correlative-καί arm is not in play here, being scoped to a καί answering καθώς where no οὕτως is expressed; with both adverb and conjunction expressed and both English words written, rule 2 splits them.

Both articles before Χριστοῦ are unrepresented under rule 23 (article before a name), and since the ASV supplies no determiner, rule 21's second half keeps the case preposition of with the noun rather than leaving a bare of on the article. Rule 57 is not in question: nothing is interposed between either article and its name.

ἡ before παράκλησις is unrepresented under rule 20 proper, not under rule 76's second arm: the genitive ἡμῶν is expressed and has been spent on nothing else, so it is the word the supplied our belongs to.
